question.text: What is the SEBI-mandated time limit for processing mutual fund redemption proceeds for liquid and overnight fund schemes?

answer.text: 1 business day from the date of redemption request
3 business days from the date of redemption request
5 business days from the date of redemption request
10 business days from the date of redemption request

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI circulars on mutual fund redemption turnaround, redemption proceeds for liquid and overnight fund schemes are required to be transferred to the unitholder within one business day (T+1) of receipt of a valid redemption request. Other open-ended schemes follow a longer dispatch cycle (typically up to T+3 business days), and SEBI specifies penal interest if redemption proceeds are not transferred within the prescribed period. The Trap: 3 business days is the broader standard for non-liquid open-ended schemes, not for liquid/overnight funds. 5 and 10 business days are not the prescribed turnarounds for liquid/overnight redemptions — 10 business days is associated with the penal-interest trigger rather than the standard timeline. The shortest, product-specific deadline applies to liquid and overnight schemes precisely because investors use them for near-cash liquidity. Note: The cited pages of the NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook (p.80, p.189, p.218-p.219) discuss redemption/repurchase, the Instant Access Facility (Rs. 50,000 / 90% cap), and the requirement to transfer redemption proceeds within a period specified by SEBI, but do not state an explicit T+1 deadline for liquid/overnight funds or a T+3 deadline for other schemes. The framing above is general SEBI circular knowledge on redemption turnaround.
